additional_info.subject: RE: ID0367654-DC/Si-D/SE [Y2/S5 313660945001] Missing Converters in DC4 CRM:00643000776
additional_info.body:
Hi Magnus,
Greetings of the day!
In relation to this power converter issue, we have checked with the help of Debug station and it seems there is an issue with power converter. Please follow the below steps for troubleshooting.
1. Checked the converter grouping in the SCB, it looks fine as per the Flex configuration.
2. Please check if the power converter are properly connection to its shelf case.
3. Check for any loose connection of any power cable or CAN communication cables of the converter and measured the voltage across it with the help of multimeter. Check the resistance across CAN communication cables.
4. Please see to the display of the power converter whether it is OFF state or ON?
5. Try swapping the power converter with the good one and if the error flag was changed to the replaced one then we can suspect that the converter is faulty.
6. If all the steps are performed and you still see the power converter are faulty, we suggest you to replace it as we can't rework to it.

additional_info.subject: Sv: ID0367654-DC/Si-D/SE [Y2/S5 313660945001] Missing Converters in DC4 CRM:00643000776
additional_info.body:
Hi
A couple of questions.
Point 3. How do you measure the voltage on the converters in a safe way and where do you want us to measure the resistance of the canbus?
Point 4. How do think that we can see the display? It’s all the way in and in the bottom? Yoy have to remember that there is no power on the converters when the doors open and we then need to disable this function to get power.
Point 5. Why do you think that this will help?
They have been working for quite a long time so why do you suspect that there is something else wrong then the converter?
I have had similar issues before and never found anything else wrong then the converter itself.
